source_documents.title: Kinetics of Excimer Electrogenerated Chemiluminescence of Pyrene and 1-Pyrenebutyricacid 2-Ethylhexylester in Acetonitrile and an Ionic Liquid, Triethylpentylphosphonium Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide

reference_evidence_units.quote: the broad PL emission with the maximum around 480 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PLQ concentration series in MeCN and the ionic liquid [P2225][TFSI].
reference_evidence_units.statement: The approximately 480 nm broad emission increases with concentration; neat PLQ is dominated by excimer emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Pyrene is a comparator; its values are not PLQ measurements.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the formation of excimers is a diffusion-controlled process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Concentration-dependent PL decay fits and diffusion coefficients from electrochemistry.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fitted excimer formation rates and diffusion-limited estimates agree; the much more viscous ionic liquid suppresses excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Diffusion-controlled intermolecular encounters are distinct from restriction of internal rotation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a 0.3−0.4 ns delay of the excimer emission in neat PLQ
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neat PLQ compared with dilute PLQ monomer emission; main text describes SI Fig. S2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: A short delayed rise is reported for neat PLQ, interpreted as an orientational rearrangement before excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The raw SI decay is not available here; do not confuse this subnanosecond formation delay with delayed fluorescence from triplet states.

reference_evidence_units.quote: four different dimer structures with stacked pyrene rings are possible
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ dimers
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PBE0/TZVp potential energy curves with assumed parallel-stacked rings, Fig. 5 and Table 3.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Three modeled PLQ configurations have an excited-state energy minimum at 3.50 angstrom; a sterically disfavored configuration shifts to 4.95 angstrom.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The stacked starting geometry is assumed to reduce cost. These are computed geometries, not an experimental crystal structure.

reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ versus pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Monomer PL lifetime and integrating-sphere yield at 10 micromolar; Table 2.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The source derives radiative and nonradiative rates and attributes the larger PLQ radiative rate to symmetry breaking by its substituent; ionic-liquid interactions also enhance the radiative rate.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Main prose gives a MeCN PLQ lifetime near 210 ns whereas Table 2 lists 198 ns. This discrepancy should be resolved before adopting a precise lifetime.

reference_evidence_units.quote: can be ascribed to the suppression of vibrational relaxations
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of inferred nonradiative rates in viscous ionic liquid and MeCN.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The authors attribute the reduced nonradiative rate in the ionic liquid to suppressed vibrational relaxation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is an indirect interpretation of rate estimates, not resolved vibrational dynamics or a general aggregation-induced RIM mechanism.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the direct formation of the monomer S1 states through the electron transfer prevails
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene ECL
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Electrogenerated radical-ion annihilation, Marcus-rate analysis and dimer energies.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The favored proposed ECL route first creates the monomer excited state by electron transfer, followed by diffusion-driven excimer formation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is electrode-driven electron transfer, not evidence for a photoinduced intramolecular PET quencher. Continuum-solvent and electronic-coupling assumptions limit the kinetic model.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a depletion around 495 nm was observed.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene ECL
reference_evidence_units.conditions: High-concentration ionic-liquid solutions under square-wave electrochemical excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The spectral depletion is attributed to reabsorption by accumulated radical anions, not a separate emitting mechanism.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This artifact is concentration- and excitation-dependent; do not turn two apparent peaks into two excited-state mechanism labels.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the authors' suppressed vibrational relaxation explanation under viscous-solvent conditions, with its indirect evidential status.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Electron transfer generates excited states in the ECL protocol. This broad ET-family assignment is conditional on electrochemical excitation, not conventional intramolecular photoinduced PET.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Excimer formation is the central explanation supported by concentration trends, kinetics and bounded dimer calculations.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Lifetime/yield-derived rates and symmetry/solvent effects support a rate-balance interpretation; reabsorption must not be misclassified as state redistribution.
